cards.explanation: The answer is swarms of locusts. Amos says the Lord GOD "…was preparing swarms of locusts just after the king’s harvest, as the late spring crop was coming up." (Amos 7:1) The timing is the sting here, friends. The crop is just coming up, and that's when the locusts show up.

The answer is True. When the locusts have eaten every green plant in the land, Amos says, "Lord GOD, please forgive!" (Amos 7:2) He doesn't wait around or argue, friends. He speaks up for the people right away.

The reason Amos gives is that Jacob is so small. Amos asks, "How will Jacob survive, since he is so small?" (Amos 7:2) That's his whole case, short and simple, friends. I wish I could make my case that tight when I'm asking for one more cookie.

The answer is False. The text says, "So the LORD relented from this plan." (Amos 7:3) Then He says, "It will not happen…" The locust plan does not go ahead, friends. Amos speaks, and the LORD relents.

The answer is False, and not by a little. Amos says the fire "…consumed the great deep and devoured the land." (Amos 7:4) It's not a small corner of the land, bakers. It reaches the great deep and the land itself.

Amos asks the Lord GOD to stop. He says, "Lord GOD, please stop! How will Jacob survive, since he is so small?" (Amos 7:5) Same worry as the first vision, and same move, friends. He goes straight to the Lord GOD and speaks up for Jacob.

The Lord GOD says, "It will not happen either…" (Amos 7:6) Just before that, the text says, "So the LORD relented from this plan." The word "either" matters, bakers. It's the second time the LORD relents after Amos speaks.

The answer is among His people Israel. The Lord says, "I am setting a plumb line among My people Israel…" (Amos 7:8) Notice the words "My people," friends. The plumb line is set right in the middle of them.

The answer is False, and it's a big change from the first two visions. The Lord says, "I will no longer spare them…" (Amos 7:8) Twice the LORD relented after Amos spoke up (Amos 7:3, 6). Here He says no more sparing, friends.

The answer is deserted. The Lord says, "The high places of Isaac will be deserted…" (Amos 7:9) That's the first thing on His list, friends. They'll sit empty, like a bakery with the lights off and nobody inside.

The answer is sword. The Lord says, "…I will rise up against the house of Jeroboam with My sword." (Amos 7:9) Watch how it gets personal, bakers. First the high places, then the sanctuaries, and now a house with a name on it.
